Analysis Without Gold Standard

Source: R/nogoldstandard.h.R
nogoldstandard.Rd

Analysis of multiple binary tests when no perfect reference exists. Implements a conditional-independence two-class latent class model, fixed-prior penalized EM point estimation with numerical refinement, and descriptive agreement with self-built reference rules. Latent classes are unlabeled, and reference-rule results are not diagnostic-accuracy estimates.

Usage

nogoldstandard(
  data,
  clinicalPreset = "none",
  test1,
  test1Positive,
  test2 = NULL,
  test2Positive,
  test3 = NULL,
  test3Positive,
  test4 = NULL,
  test4Positive,
  test5 = NULL,
  test5Positive,
  method = "latent_class",
  bootstrap = FALSE,
  nboot = 1000,
  alpha = 0.05,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = 0,
  showSummary = FALSE,
  showMethodGuide = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

The data as a data frame.

clinicalPreset

Illustrative scenario examples only. They do not change analysis settings and are not clinical guides, validated recommendations, or substitutes for a study-specific analysis plan.

test1

First diagnostic test variable.

test1Positive

The positive level for Test 1.

test2

Second diagnostic test variable.

test2Positive

The positive level for Test 2.

test3

Third diagnostic test variable (optional).

test3Positive

The positive level for Test 3.

test4

Fourth diagnostic test variable (optional).

test4Positive

The positive level for Test 4.

test5

Fifth diagnostic test variable (optional).

test5Positive

The positive level for Test 5.

method

Method for analyzing tests without a gold standard. Composite Reference uses a strict majority (more than half positive); ties with an even number of tests are classified as rule negative.

bootstrap

Calculate case-resampling percentile confidence intervals. For latent-class and penalized-EM models, confidence intervals are reported only when this option is enabled because ordinary binomial intervals do not account for latent-variable estimation. Latent intervals require a converged, reportable full-sample fit and at least 20 finite estimates for each interval. Coverage is approximate and may be poor with small samples, boundaries or weak identification; case resampling assumes independent rows.

nboot

Number of bootstrap samples for confidence intervals.

alpha

Alpha level for confidence intervals.

verbose

Show detailed analysis diagnostics, including convergence, random starts, exclusions, and bootstrap failures when bootstrap intervals are enabled.

seed

Base random seed for the reproducible latent-class multi-start search and bootstrap resampling. Each start is offset from this base, so changing it shifts the whole reproducible sequence; the default (0) reproduces the previous behavior.

showSummary

Show an optional plain-language summary. The summary describes the fitted quantities and their assumptions; it is not clinical guidance.

showMethodGuide

Show an optional educational guide to the available methods. The scenarios are illustrative examples, not clinical guides or validated recommendations.

Value

A results object containing:

results$noticesa preformatted
results$instructionsa html
results$agreement_statsa table
results$clinical_summarya html
results$method_guidea html
results$prevalencea table
results$test_metricsa table
results$model_fita table
results$conditional_dependenceLatent class analysis assumes the tests are conditionally independent within each latent class. For each pair this compares the observed two-way table with the one implied by the fitted model. A residual above 3.84 is descriptive evidence against conditional independence, but this squared statistic does not identify the direction or cause of dependence and cannot determine the direction of bias in the fitted parameters. With three tests the nominal residual degrees of freedom are zero, but exact fit is not guaranteed. Residuals remain descriptive and do not provide a formal chi-squared test or establish identifiability.
results$diagnosticsDetail of how the estimates were produced: sample size, method, convergence, number of random starts used, and bootstrap failures. Shown only when Verbose output is enabled.
results$crosstaba table
results$agreement_plotan image

Tables can be converted to data frames with asDF or as.data.frame. For example:

results$agreement_stats$asDF

as.data.frame(results$agreement_stats)
